To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) The plant ADPGlc pathway appears to be the major if not sole pathway for synthesis of starch in plants.

the plant ADPglucose pyrophosphorylase (ADPGlc synthetse) is composed of two subunits and that the smaller subunit contains the binding site for the activator, 2PGA, and that the larger subunits contains the substrate, ATP, binding site.
the plant ADPglucose (ADPGlc) synthetase is a homodimer of two dissimilar subunits.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the molecular mechanism of regulation of starch biosynthesis in plants.
the regulation of the biosynthetic enzymes involved in starch synthesis.
the isolation, purification, characterization and cloning of the enzymes involved in starch synthesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the plant ADPglucose pathway is the major, if not the only pathway for starch biosynthesis in plants.

the ADPGlcsynthesizing system is a complex enzyme composed of two different peptide chains which are products of two different structural genes and that the smaller subunit is responsible for the 3PGA activation and the larger subunit is responsible in part for the binding of the ATP.
the biosynthetic reactions involved in the synthesis of starch are catalyzed respectively by ADPglc synthetase, starch synthase and branching enzyme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ADPGlc synthase in higher plants is an oligomeric enzyme composed of two subunits, the 51 kD subunit being the activator binding site and the 54 kDa being the substrate binding site.

the ADPGIc pathway is the sole pathway for the synthesis of starch in higher plants, the ADPGI c synthetase is a heterodimer of two different subunit masses, the smaller subunit has an activator binding site, the larger subunit participates in the binding and activation of the substrate, and the enzyme is completely localized in the chloroplasts of leaves and the amylopasts of non-photosynthetlc tissues.
we have isolated and characterized the ADPGlc synthesis enzyme from spinach leaf, maize endosperm, potato tuber, Arabidopsis thaliana leaf and rice endosperm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ADPGIc synthetase is a hetero-octameric enzyme composed of four 51 kDa and four 54 kDa polypeptides and that the 3PGA binding site is located on the 51 kD subunit.
the ADPGIc synthetase of plants, whether photosynthetic or not, is composed of 2 subunits and that the subunits are products of different genes.
the biosynthetic enzymes for starch biosynthesis are completely localized in subcellular compartments where starch is formed, the chloroplasts of leaves and the amylopasts of endosperm.
